cs.t: I own a Boox Note. Onyx shamelessly uses shill accounts on reddit and twitter to advertise their products. And yes, they are GPL violators. My Boox isn't all terrible, but I would strongly suggest people check out Supernote or Remarkable instead. Both have their issues, but don't buy a Boox.
cs.th: Onyx BOOX Nova3 Color, the first color ereader supports writing

cs.t: I recently bought a Supernote which is an e-ink tablet.  I've had it a few months now and haven't written in a notebook since I got it.  I got a daily planner template for it so use it daily.  I also sketch out project ideas, etc.  It will do ebooks as well but I have a Kindle so don't use it for that.
cs.th: Ask HN: Tablet recommendations for reading and taking notes

cs.t: I would recommend Supernote instead of Remarkable, as that can sync the notes via Obsidian.
cs.th: Ask HN: What are your most regretted tech purchases?

cs.t: Landscape mode would make sense, if scrolling on eInk wasn't completely awful. I can sometimes deal with it on really light websites like Wikipedia, but I just prefer not to. I will say that my supernote really is just a digital notepad. I keep all my work to do lists organized on it. But since it's Android and supports side loading apps, I have the Kobo app and read a ton on it even without a backlight.

I work remotely, and when trying to discuss concepts with others, I frequently doodle things out with pen and paper (just like I used to on a whiteboard in an office).  Having a Supernote means I can share my diagrams live on the call, just like a real whiteboard, which in turn makes it easier to communicate with my coworkers. I've used all kinds of drawing apps on the web previously, and the extra impedance of the mouse/canvas/tool selection/whatever frustrates the whole process.
